newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh's Hasina welcomes new Indian PM Gujral.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh's Hasina welcomes new Indian PM Gujral.

text.p: Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Monday sent a warm greeting to her new Indian counterpart, Inder Kumar Gujral, calling him a "genuine friend" of her country.

"We regard you as a genuine friend of Bangladesh and hold you in high esteem for your personal interest in and valuable contribution to promotion and strengthening of Bangladesh-India friendship and cooperation," Hasina said in a message to Gujral.

"We recall with a sense of appreciation that the significant developments in relations between our two countries during the past few months had been an outcome of the initiatives of I.K. Gujral," she said in her message soon after returning to Dhaka from her Haj pilgrimage to Mecca.
Hasina said friendship and cooperation between Dhaka and New Delhi would "grow from strength to strength" during Gujral's premiership.

Gujral was sworn in on Monday as the country's 12th prime minister since independence in 1947. He was foreign minister in the United Front coalition of former prime minister H.D. Deve Gowda, whose government fell earlier this month.
Earlier, Bangladeshis from all walks of life welcomed Gujral's appointment, describing him as moderate, secularist, a trusted friend, man of vision and a great choice.
In the country's first official comment, Foreign Minister Abdus Samad Azad said: "I wish him all success in his new responsibility in service to his nation."

Zillur Rahman, general secretary of Bangladesh's ruling Awami League, said: "We are delighted over the peaceful resolution of India's political problem and it is more heartening that a person like I.K. Gujral is becoming the new prime minister."
Abdul Mannan Bhuiyan, seceretary-general of the main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party, also welcomed Gujral in his new position.
"There could not have been a better instance of reason and far sight emerging from a milieu of impending chaos," said Dhaka's daily Star in an editorial comment.
"The emergence of Mr Gujral at the executive acme of India should also usher in a new era of cooperation in the region."

The daily Independent said: "As foreign minister in the outgoing Deve Gowda government, Gujral was instrumental in articulating a pragmatic foreign policy towards its neighbours, including Bangladesh.

"As Prime Minister, Gujral will be in a position to pursue his doctrine with more vigour. We hope Prime Minister Gujral will spare no efforts to take his foreign policy initiative to its logical conclusion."
The daily Banglabazar Patrika described Gujral as a "tested friend of Bangladesh", and said his nomination as prime minister had come as a relief to Bangladesh.
Yusuf Abdullah Harun, president of the Federation of Bangladesh Chamber of Commerce and Industry, said "Mr Gujral's choice is a good news for us and possibly for all of India's neighbours."

During the 10-month rule of outgoing Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, Bangladesh and India signed a landmark 30-year river sharing treaty and reached agreements to repatriate Bangladeshi tribal refugees from India and jointly to fight insurgencies.
The Bangladesh government and officials give much of the credit for the accords to Gujral.
